newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat to cut January car output with layoffs.
newsitem.headline: Fiat to cut January car output with layoffs.

text.p: Fiat Auto SpA said it plans to trim vehicle production in January by 10,300 units with temporary layoffs.

The rolling layoffs in the four weeks from January 7 to February 2 will involve workers at plants at Pomigliano, Rivalta, Arese and Cassino, affecting the production of the Alfa 155, Gtv and Spider, Lancia Delta and Dedra, and Fiat Bravo and Brava.
Fiat has for years resorted to temporary layoffs, generally on a month-by-month basis, in order to trim output due to the state of Italy's depressed car market.
The whole European car market hit the floor in 1993 but while other markets recovered, Italy has lagged behind.
Although Fiat sales are doing well in Europe outside Italy, its share of the domestic market fell to 45.63 percent in November from 48.75 percent in November 1995.
